hook: The fastest way to lose power in any negotiation is to speak first after the price is named.
full_script: The fastest way to lose power in any negotiation is to speak first after the price is named. When an offer is put on the table, an amateur rushes to fill the awkward silence with justifications, discounts, and nervous laughter. Silence is psychological pressure. The human brain interprets stillness as absolute confidence, and nervous chatter as weakness. He who speaks first absorbs the tension; he who stays quiet forces the other side to negotiate against themselves. Words are not leverage; restraint is. You reveal your desperation the moment you apologize for what you deserve. Learn to sit inside the discomfort of dead silence. The master moves with zero hurry, and lets the amateur break first.
